display.title: Episode 379: Judge for a Day, Chapter 1
display.summary_short: Pirkei Avos teaches that Hashem creates the world anew every moment; story time begins 'Judge for a Day', in which honest Beryl the butcher is accused of theft; and mitzvah time introduces Havdalah.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the last weeks of Sefiras HaOmer 5749, as Shavuos approaches. Uncle Yossi explains the first Mishnah of the fifth chapter of Pirkei Avos: the world was created with ten sayings. Unlike a carpenter, whose chair stands without him, Hashem creates the world from nothing every moment, just as a bulb shines only while the current flows, so we should thank Him with Torah and mitzvos. Two sisters from a girls' school lead the Shema and recite 'Kol Yisrael' from the Twelve Pesukim. Story time begins 'Judge for a Day': Label, a bright and well-mannered yeshiva boy, hears that honest Beryl the butcher has been accused by Ivan, a sly tailor, of stealing exactly 365 gold coins hidden under his floorboard. Beryl turns to Tehillim, and Label prays for a way to help, and the chapter stops there. In mitzvah time, children learn what Havdalah means, when it is made, and what goes into a Havdalah kit, with a quiz contest. The show ends with Shabbos candle times.
display.lesson: Hashem creates and sustains the world every moment, so we owe Him our thanks through Torah, mitzvos and good midos.
